item.title: The Human Intellectual Idea Stamp: A Proposal to Record Human Origination of Research Ideas
item.description:
Authors: Sridhar Chimalakonda

Source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

Why included: Canadian-affiliated author or institution

Abstract: Today, artificial intelligence (AI) is present in every part of the research lifecycle. It suggests research questions, retrieves and summarizes literature, implements and runs studies, drafts manuscripts, and reviews the manuscripts of others. Submission volumes have grown sharply over the same period. AAAI received 23,680 submissions to its main technical track in 2026, around eighty percent more than the previous year. Many publishers now require authors to disclose how AI was used, including which tools were involved. Our question is different. If AI can suggest, implement, write, and review, what should a researcher focus on? We take the answer to be the intellectual act at the core of research: deciding what question is worth asking, why, and what idea might answer it. item.title: Distinguishability of Q5 Deviations via Phase-Cycling Invariants
item.description:
Authors: Craig Edwin Holdway

Source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

Why included: Canadian-affiliated author or institution

Abstract: T73 develops a phase-cycling discriminator for Q5-consistent deviations that cannot be identified from a single interference scan. Building on T72, which shows that any first-harmonic residual can be absorbed by refitting the ordinary fringe parameters, T73 demonstrates that the lost information can survive in the constrained transformation law across multiple controlled phase settings. The theorem considers four scans separated by externally controlled \(\pi/2\) phase offsets and replaces independent per-scan refitting with a single jointly constrained fit across all four settings. For these offsets, the ordinary fringe model occupies one two-dimensional phase-cycling chirality subspace, while the opposite chirality subspace is exactly orthogonal to it. item.description:
Authors: Tobechukwu Ohaka, Tizazu H. Mekonnen

Source: ACS Applied Polymer Materials

Why included: Canadian-affiliated author or institution

Abstract: Abstract Recycling sulfur-cross-linked natural rubber (NR) to enhance its sustainability and reduce waste remains challenging due to its permanent network and existing devulcanization approaches that are energy-intensive and inconsistent and risk backbone degradation. Here, we introduce a recyclable thermoreversible covalent adaptable network (CAN) based on furan-maleimide Diels–Alder (DA) chemistry, synthesized directly through batch mechanochemical processing. NR was functionalized with furfurylamine (FFA) and cross-linked in situ with bismaleimide (BM) to form dynamic DA bonds, and the resulting networks were characterized via VT-FTIR, XPS, DMA, DSC, and tensile testing to assess structural, thermal, and mechanical properties. item.title: Spatiotemporal Computer-Vision Measurement of Flocculation and Settling: A Preliminary Kaolin–Polymer Model
item.description:
Authors: Melinda B. Chu

Source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

Why included: Canadian-affiliated author or institution

Abstract: Coagulation, flocculation, clarification, and settling are dynamic water-treatment processes that generate spatially and temporally evolving optical states. Conventional image-analysis approaches can characterize individual flocs, particle dimensions, or discrete image features; however, the entire liquid field may also contain information relevant to process-state measurement. This technical note presents a preliminary spatiotemporal computer-vision approach to flocculation and settling using a controlled kaolin suspension and a commercial charged-polymer clarifier. Side-view smartphone images were acquired at 0, 5, 10, 20, 30, and 60 minutes following polymer addition. item.description:
Authors: Marie-Line Kühn, Carlotta Lupatelli, Blandine Madji Hounoum, Aurélie Séassau, Anne-Sophie Gay, Sophie Pagnotta, François Orange, Ilaria Bassani et al.

Source: bioRxiv (Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory)

Why included: Canadian-affiliated author or institution

Abstract: Zoospores are unicellular, wall-less and flagellated cells produced by a number of eukaryotic microorganisms. They allow microbial dispersion, enable the search and location for new sources of nutrients where they aggregate, initiate pathogen-host interactions and communication within microbiota. Little is known about their ability to release bioactive extracellular vesicles (EVs) supporting these adaptations. Here we used electron microscopy to establish that in the biflagellate zoospores of the heterokont and phytopathogenic species Phytophthora parasitica, EV biogenesis occurs from vesicles budding either at cell body plasma membrane or at the front flagellum, in particular from the tubular mastigonemes. Abstract: Suspended solids alter the optical properties of water through attenuation, scattering, particulate distribution, and spatial heterogeneity. Abstract: Due to regional effects of typhoon poleward migration and terrain influences, it is important to investigate the impacts of typhoon rainfall (TR) changes on total rainfall (R) across different timescales and their spatial heterogeneity. item.title: Longitudinal changes in control energy of brain networks in older adults at familial risk for Alzheimers disease
item.description:
Authors: Paulina Skolasinska, Alfie Wearn, Daniel O'Sullivan, Isabella Stallworthy, Julia K. Brynildsen, Ilana R. Leppert, Christine L Tardif, Gary R. Turner et al.

Source: bioRxiv (Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory)

Why included: Canadian-affiliated author or institution

Abstract: The ability of structural brain networks to control neural dynamics is affected by healthy and pathological aging, including Alzheimers disease (AD). According to network control theory, transitions between functional brain states incur energetic costs. How these costs change longitudinally with aging remains unknown. Here, in 279 older adults at familial risk for AD, control energy increased longitudinally for state maintenance and transitions between sensorimotor and attentional networks, while decreasing for another sensorimotor—attentional transition. Changes in transition costs between higher-order networks were associated with cognitive performance: greater DorsAttn—Executive cost was associated with poorer immediate memory, while lower Executive—Def+Lim cost was associated with poorer attention. Higher plasma p-tau181 was associated with lower DorsAttn—Def+Lim transition cost....

item.title: DiffDose: Differentiable Programming for Personalized Dose-Regimen Optimal Control
item.description:
Authors: Shayan Hajhashemi, Amin Emad, Morgan Craig

Source: bioRxiv (Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory)

Why included: Canadian-affiliated author or institution

Abstract: Dose-regimen design requires choosing how much drug to give, when to give it, and how treatment should vary across patients. Mechanistic pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) and quantitative systems pharmacology (QSP) models can predict treatment responses, but optimizing dosing inputs depends on model-specific sensitivity derivations or derivative-free search. Here, we introduce DiffDose, a differentiable programming framework for mechanistic open-loop dose-regimen optimization that uses automatic differentiation (AD) to handle clinically interpretable dose amounts and administration times as differentiable controls. Authors: Nicola Veronese, Luisa Solimando, Marco Solmi, Nasser Al-Daghri, Shaun Sabico

Source: Aging Clinical and Experimental Research

Why included: Canadian-affiliated author or institution

Abstract: Effective postoperative pain management is crucial for surgical recovery, yet opioid-based therapies carry significant risks of addiction and adverse effects. Celecoxib, a selective COX-2 inhibitor, has emerged as a promising non-opioid alternative within multimodal analgesic protocols. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to synthesize current evidence regarding the efficacy and safety of celecoxib specifically for major orthopedic surgeries. Following a PROSPERO-registered protocol, researchers searched major databases through 09th September 2025 for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) involving adults undergoing major orthopedic procedures. The primary outcome was postoperative pain intensity at 1, 3, 5, and 7 days. Data synthesis utilized standardized mean differences (SMD) and random-effects models. item.title: Hybridized advisory system: ministerial advisors and donor co-principalship in developing countries
item.description:
Authors: Kiflie Worku Angaw

Source: Policy Design and Practice

Why included: Canadian-affiliated author or institution

Abstract: Ministerial advisors have become increasingly prominent actors in policy advisory systems, yet existing scholarship draws largely from the Global North, leaving significant gaps in understanding their roles in developing countries. Drawing on primary data, this study examines recruitment, positioning, and policy influence of ministerial advisors in the developing country context. The findings reveal that ministerial advisory roles are institutionalized through what this study theorizes as a hybridized advisory system (HAS), a configuration in which donors function as external advisory actors and as co-principals who define advisory mandates, recruit and finance ministerial advisors, and exercise veto-like authority alongside political principals. Once embedded in government, ministerial advisors exert substantial influence over policy design and implementation. Their relationships with...

Source: Discover Neuroscience

Why included: Canadian-affiliated author or institution

Abstract: Prenatal cannabis exposure (PCE) is associated with neurocognitive impairments in childhood, but the underlying neurodevelopmental process remains unclear. In analysis of a subset of data from a prospective cohort of children (age 7–8 years, n = 56) with and without PCE in the US, we find that PCE is associated with lower performance on a task of working memory ability, although this association was attenuated (and non-significant) after controlling for prenatal tobacco exposure. Differences between exposure groups were not apparent on several other cognitive tasks. Compared to unexposed peers, children with PCE also show reductions in a multivariate metric of cortical thickness predominantly within the frontal and parietal cortices when accounting for confounding variables. item.title: The Thinness Index: A Transport-Based Diagnostic for Chaos in Engineered and Natural Systems
item.description:
Authors: Doug Doucette

Source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

Why included: Canadian-affiliated author or institution

Abstract: The paper addresses an ambiguity in chaos diagnostics. A positive Lyapunov exponent establishes local instability and the failure of exact point prediction, but it does not show whether chaotic motion can carry a system across the boundary that defines operational failure. The authors distinguish thin chaos, where local instability remains confined, from thick chaos, where chaotic transport becomes failure-relevant, with transitional chaos as the warning regime between them. To make this distinction operational, they introduce the thinness index, which compares the amount of chaotic transport in a coherence-relevant variable over a chosen timescale with the displacement required to reach failure. The paper develops a step-by-step protocol: define an operational timescale, measure local instability, identify a coherent region, choose a transport variable, estimate chaotic transport,...

Abstract: INTRODUCTION: Cognitively stimulating activity (CSA) is associated with cognitive health, but whether associations with cognitive change differ by life stage and sex remains unclear. METHODS: Data were drawn from Rush cohorts. Participants were 2,614 adults aged 65 years and older (1,965 females; 649 males). Linear mixed-effects models examined global cognition and five domains, adjusting for age, education, and cognitive diagnosis. Sex-engagement-time interactions were tested with false discovery rate correction. item.title: Quasi-Constitutionality and Indigenous-State Treaties in Australia
item.description:
Authors: Hobbs, Harry ; https://orcid.org/0000-0001-9903-6908, Taylor, Alice

Source: UNSWorks (University of New South Wales, Sydney, Australia)

Why included: Canadian-affiliated author or institution; Canada-related term in abstract: canada, victoria

Abstract: The Statewide Treaty negotiated between the First Peoples Assembly of Victoria and the Victorian government is momentous. However, the Statewide Treaty Bill 2025 (Vic), which implements the agreement, is an ordinary piece of legislation subject to the ordinary rules of statutory interpretation and implied repeal. Drawing on jurisprudence from Canada, the United Kingdom and scholarship from the United States, we argue that the anticipated Statewide Treaty Act should properly be understood as ‘quasi-constitutional’ because it: (i) shapes the character of Victoria in moral and legal ways, (ii) is understood within the broader community as a statute of great importance, and (iii) regulates the institutions and powers of the state. This designation has important legal and expressive implications which supports the status and prominence of Indigenous-State treaties.
